subject: URGENT: StormRetail - sudden egress latency & 5xx spike (needs action)
messages:
From: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@stormretail.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: ops-team@stormretail.com
Date: Sat, 11 May 2029 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden increase in token latency and 503 errors from Redwood API

Hi Marissa —

We started seeing a sharp increase in 95th/99th percentile latencies and a non-trivial 5xx rate in our production checkout flow starting ~05:45 PDT. Symptoms:
- 95th latency up from ~120ms to ~2.4s
- Error rate (502/503) ~6% across requests to the /generate endpoint
- Throughput dropped ~30% (retries + backpressure on our side)

This is affecting live checkout for a portion of customers in us-west and is causing abandoned carts. Our ops team is seeing DNS timeouts when resolving your edge hostnames (redwood-edge-us-west.prod). We captured traces and the attached logs.

Can the Redwood team triage immediately? If this is on your side, please advise on fallback steps — we may need to switch to the hosted fallback region or temporarily disable VPC peering to see impact. This is causing P1-level customer impact.

Attachments: stormretail_api_errors_20290511.zip (sample 5xx traces, agent logs), storm_traceroute_11may.txt

- Carlos
Carlos Vega
Head of Platform Ops
StormRetail
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@stormretail.com>, ops-team@stormretail.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 11 May 2029 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden increase in token latency and 503 errors from Redwood API

Carlos — thanks for the flag and the attachments. We’re on it. Immediate plan: 
1) Collect active traceroutes / tcpdumps from your egress and our edge (please confirm the traceroute file is the one attached).
2) Check VPC peering metrics and NAT gateway utilization for your VPC in us-west — Vivek, can you pull peering telemetry + NAT/ENI metrics?
3) If DNS failures persist, we can:
   - enable DNS fallback to our regional resolver (non-VPC) for a short canary window, and/or
   - shift ~10% of traffic to hosted-us-west-2 for 30m while we investigate.

Please share any additional traceroutes/pcaps; we’ll coordinate a short triage call if needed. I’ll keep execs updated if this escalates.

Meeting: https://meet.redwood.com/j/triage-20290511 (standby)

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@stormretail.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: ops-team@stormretail.com
Date: Sat, 11 May 2029 08:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden increase in token latency and 503 errors from Redwood API

On Sat, May 11, 2029 at 8:20 AM PDT Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Carlos — thanks for the flag and the attachments. We’re on it. Immediate plan: 
> 1) Collect active traceroutes / tcpdumps from your egress and our edge ...

Attached the traceroute and a small packet capture from our edge NAT (storm_traceroute_11may.txt is included in the zip). Key excerpts from our ops engineer:
- DNS timeouts to redwood-edge-us-west.prod at 05:46:12-05:46:22 (multiple retries)
- Several SYN retransmits toward 34.87.XX.XX (your egress IP) followed by 3-way handshake delays
- No apparent issues inside our VPC prior to the NAT/gateway hop

We’re ready to initiate the fallback to hosted region if you confirm it’s safe. We need an ETA for the short mitigation window so we can coordinate on our side (cookie/session stickiness, etc.).

- Carlos
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: carlos.vega@stormretail.com
Date: Sat, 11 May 2029 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec brief & immediate mitigations — suspected egress path congestion / NAT exhaustion

Marissa / Rishi — quick escalation note for the thread and exec visibility. Summary: StormRetail reports DNS timeouts and SYN retries hitting our edge for a subset of flows originating from their peered VPC. Early telemetry suggests transient NAT exhaustion or an intermediary transit device experiencing high connection churn in the customer egress path (not a code regression in our runtime).

Why we think this:
- Customer traceroutes show delayed responses after their NAT/gateway hop; our edge ingress shows retries and delayed socket accept times aligned with the same interval.
- CDN/edge health is green overall; model CPU and GPU queues not saturated.

Proposed immediate mitigations (implementable in 15–30m):
- Enable DNS fallback to Redwood regional resolver (non-peered path) for StormRetail’s tenant for a 30m canary.
- Temporarily shift 10–15% of their production traffic to hosted-us-west-2 to relieve the peered path while preserving capacity.
- BGP reroute / announce alternative peering prefix if customer requests it (requires change window).

Operational asks: Rishi — can your team prepare the traffic-shift canary config and the monitoring runbook? Marissa — please confirm the customer approval to do a 30m fallback. I’ll prepare a one-page exec brief (attached).

Attachments: redwood_exec_brief_20290511.pdf
Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/NETOPS-2319

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Production Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@stormretail.com>, ops-team@stormretail.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 11 May 2029 10:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden increase in token latency and 503 errors from Redwood API

Carlos — thanks for the quick signal and for approving the canary. We ran the DNS fallback + 10% traffic shift starting 09:30 PDT as a canary. Observations during canary window: 
- 95th latency back down to ~140–180ms for canary traffic
- 5xx rate for canary traffic dropped to ~0.3%
- Full rollback not required; canary validated the hypothesis that the peered path was the source of impact.

Next steps:
- We recommend scheduling an operational window with your network team to investigate NAT gateway sizing / intermediate transit device behavior.
- We’ll keep the fallback in place for 2 hours and then either remove or extend based on your network team's findings.

If you want us to open a joint support ticket with your cloud provider for the NAT behavior, I can coordinate. Thank you and please ping if anything regresses — we’ll keep the triage call on hold for 30m.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Attachments: redwood_exec_brief_20290511.pdf
